trust_decision.summary: The uncompressed length declared in an untrusted Snappy header (parsed by native code) is trusted, unchecked, to size Java heap/direct allocations; the decision lives in the Snappy.uncompressedLength overloads and their callers in Snappy, SnappyInputStream and SnappyFramedInputStream.

landing_point.why: Snappy.uncompress(byte[]) is the headline API and allocates new byte[Snappy.uncompressedLength(input)] directly from the header value.

fix_sites.entry_point: SnappyFramedInputStream.read() -> ensureBuffer (allocation from declared length, fixed via Snappy.uncompressedLength(ByteBuffer))

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/main/java/org/xerial/snappy/SnappyFramedInputStream.java:520-559 (framing-format reader: skippable-chunk recursion at :528-531 and declared-length allocation at :553-559, a separate class from the Snappy facade and SnappyInputStream)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The framing format is a separate, spec-defined stream class with its own chunk-length limit (24-bit header), so a solver fixing Snappy.uncompress can argue it is a neighbouring feature; for SnappyInputStream the 512 MiB maxChunkSize cap and the 'concatenated streams are a supported feature' argument both invite leaving the routes alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Highly compressible input (e.g. all zeros, ~21x ratio) and empty input must still decompress, so a declared-length bound tighter than 64/3 of the compressed size breaks legitimate data; concatenated SnappyOutputStream streams and skippable/padding frames must keep being accepted.

O7_producer.where: Declared length is produced by the native header parser SnappyNative.uncompressedLength (src/main/java/org/xerial/snappy/SnappyNative.java:82-90); none of the listed producer kinds applies

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SnappyInputStream.hasNextChunk recurses once per concatenated 16-byte magic header, the same unbounded-recursion shape the fix removed from the framed reader's skip path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Concatenated streams are a documented legitimate feature, and the published fix only touched skippable chunks in the framing-format class.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file from landing point and from the framed fix site; same package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SnappyInputStream allocates new byte[chunkSize] from a 4-byte chunk header (default cap 512 MiB) before reading any chunk data.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Already bounded by the configurable maxChunkSize (SnappyInputStream.java:39, :444), so it looks intentionally limited.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file from landing point; same package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SnappyFramedInputStream allocates direct and array buffers sized from the 24-bit frame length (and maxCompressedLength of it) before the frame body is read; the framing spec caps chunks far lower.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The 24-bit length caps it at 16 MiB, so it can be argued to be bounded already.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file from landing point; same package; helper at SnappyFramedInputStream.java:243-261

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A typed unshuffle+uncompress helper sizing its output from Snappy's declared length via impl directly instead of the checked facade.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: BitShuffle already exposes per-type array helpers next to native calls; a maintainer adding a fused decompress helper would naturally call the native API for speed.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: readFully path for headerless Snappy.compress output computing the length with a private helper that calls impl.uncompressedLength directly.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pinned uncompressedLength(byte[]) overload already does exactly this bypass (Snappy.java:656-659), so the pattern exists in the codebase.

O9_family: CWE-789 memory allocation with excessive size value from untrusted declared length (plus stack-exhaustion recursion in stream readers)

O10_build.toolchain: sbt (build.sbt, project/plugins.sbt); prebuilt native library bundled at src/main/resources/org/xerial/snappy/native/Linux/x86_64/libsnappyjava.so, so no C++ build needed for Linux x86_64

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a fixed max-size or ratio check only in Snappy.uncompress(byte[]) / the 3-arg uncompressedLength, missing the 1-arg overload that bypasses it, the ByteBuffer/address overloads and both stream readers.

out_of_scope_notes: Raw-address APIs Snappy.rawUncompress(long,long,long) and rawCompress(long,long,long) (src/main/java/org/xerial/snappy/Snappy.java:418-437) pass caller pointers to native code with no destination-capacity check; this is memory safety by design, not this allocation advisory.
The fix also adds output-space and input-range checks on compress paths (fix.diff:40, :78-79); that is memory-safety hardening alongside the DoS fix, other issues referenced in the test file.
